To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermoelectric figure of merit of GNRs can be increased by nanostructuring, and that the best results are obtained for mixed zigzag and armachair GNRs with a few vacancies.

(1) GNRs can be nanostructured so as to enhance their thermoelectric properties; (2) the edge orientation of the GNRs plays a key role in the transport properties; (3) the presence of vacancies in the GNRs can also enhance the thermoelectric properties.
the thermoelectric performance of graphene nanoribbon can be enhanced by patterning them properly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of nanoscale thermoelectrics.
the design of nanostructures for energy applications.
the study of the transport properties of graphene nanosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of the edge orientation effects with the resonant tunneling effects in GNRs allows to achieve high values of the thermoelectric factor at room temperature.

the thermoelectric properties of graphene nanobridges can be tailored by a proper choice of the ribbon width, edge orientation, edge roughness, vacancies or impurities, which allows the design of nano-structures with high ZT factor of merit.
the nanostructuration of GNRs is a promising approach to achieve high thermoelectric performances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nanostructuration of graphene nanoribbon can be a promising way to enhance thermoelectric properties.
we have developed a new strategy to improve the thermoelectric properties of graphene nanribbons.
the thermoelectric properties of graphene nanribbons can be tailored by nanostructuring the edges and/or by introducing vacancies.

nanostructuration of graphene nanoribbon can be used to enhance their thermoelectric performance.
nanostructuring of graphene is a promising strategy for the design of thermoelectric devices.
